name: GitHub
description: Read and manage repos, issues, and PRs from GitHub — via GitHub's official hosted MCP server.
note: Official GitHub-hosted remote server — nothing to install locally. On first use Claude Code opens a browser to sign in to GitHub (OAuth); no token to manage. Works with any GitHub account.
package: GitHub-hosted remote MCP server (no local install)
dataNote: Connects to GitHub's hosted MCP server (api.githubcopilot.com) using your authorized GitHub account; the model can read and manage the repos, issues, and PRs you grant access to.

name: Filesystem
description: Give Claude scoped read/write access to a local directory.
note: Edit the path arg in .mcp.json to the directory you want to expose.
dataNote: Runs locally with no network calls, but exposes the configured directory's files to the AI model.

name: Playwright
description: Drive a real browser for UI QA, screenshots, and accessibility checks.
dataNote: Downloads browser binaries on first run and navigates to URLs you or the model open.

name: Context7
description: Pull up-to-date, version-specific docs for libraries and frameworks.
dataNote: Sends the library names/queries you look up to Context7's hosted service.

name: Sequential Thinking
description: Structured step-by-step reasoning scratchpad for hard problems.
dataNote: Runs locally; a reasoning scratchpad with no external calls.

name: Roblox Studio
description: Connect an AI client to a live Roblox Studio session — explore the data model, write Luau, and run/test in play mode.
note: Official Roblox Studio MCP is a local bridge (Studio plugin + a standalone Rust server, or Studio's built-in server) and needs separate setup. Installing here adds a template entry to .mcp.json — replace the command with your built server path per Roblox's docs.
package: Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server (standalone Rust server) or Roblox Studio's built-in MCP server
dataNote: Bridges an AI client to your local Roblox Studio session; the AI can read your place's data model and write/run Luau code in it.

name: UEFN Bridge (Trashbyrd's Power Tools)
description: Live UEFN editor control from Claude — read/set actor properties, run audits, and browse materials, textures, and the level via Trashbyrd's Power Tools.
note: Local bridge — runs on your machine and only talks to your open UEFN session via temp-file IPC (no external calls). The MCP server is bundled with this extension (path resolves automatically on install). Prereqs: Node.js on your PATH (the server runs via `node`), and Trashbyrd's Power Tools' Python bridge installed in your UEFN project (Content/Python) and started in-editor. Both sides default to %TEMP%/uefn_bridge (machine-agnostic); for a custom dir set UEFN_BRIDGE_DIR for both UEFN and this server.
dataNote: Runs locally; bridges Claude to your open UEFN session over temp-file IPC. No external/network calls.

name: Unreal Engine MCP (Official · UE 5.8+)
description: Epic's official in-editor MCP server, built into Unreal Editor 5.8+. Enable the "Unreal MCP" plugin and toggle Auto Start Server in Editor Preferences, then connect over HTTP/SSE. For general Unreal Engine projects — distinct from the UEFN Bridge above, which targets UEFN/Fortnite.
note: Built into the Unreal Editor — no external bridge process. Enable via Edit > Plugins > "Unreal MCP", then Edit > Editor Preferences > General > Model Context Protocol > toggle "Auto Start Server". The editor can also auto-generate a client config via the console command: ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig ClaudeCode. Endpoint, port, and path are configurable in Editor Preferences.
dataNote: Local HTTP/SSE connection to your own running Unreal Editor (127.0.0.1, no auth by default). No external/network calls beyond your machine.

name: Blender
description: Live Blender viewport/scene control from Claude — read and modify objects, materials, and run Python (bpy) in your open Blender session.
note: Local stdio MCP server launched via `uvx blender-mcp`. Prereqs: Blender 4.x with the official Blender MCP add-on installed (drag-and-drop the add-on from https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/ into Blender, enable it, and start the MCP panel inside Blender), plus the `uv` package manager (provides `uvx`) and Python 3.10+. The server connects to the Blender add-on over a local socket (env vars BLENDER_HOST, default localhost; BLENDER_PORT, default 9876).
dataNote: Runs locally; bridges Claude to your open Blender session over a local socket (default port 9876). No external/network calls.

name: Codex (OpenAI)
description: Adversarial review and second-opinion queries from OpenAI's Codex CLI, running as an MCP server — a non-Anthropic model for cross-checking plans, diffs, and reasoning. Exposes `codex` (new session) and `codex-reply` (continue a session) tools.
note: Local stdio MCP server launched via `codex mcp-server`. Auth is via a ChatGPT subscription (shared rolling 5-hour quota across CLI/web/IDE use), not a metered API key — sign in once with `codex login`. The launch args below pin model and reasoning effort and set safe defaults for approval-policy and sandbox so this entry never silently inherits your global ~/.codex/config.toml (which may pin an expensive model at high reasoning effort). These are launch-time config.toml overrides (`-c key=value`, applied before the `mcp-server` subcommand); they set the SERVER's baked-in defaults, not a hard ceiling — the `codex` tool's own per-call `sandbox`/`approval-policy`/`model` arguments can still override them at call time, so a caller (or an untrusted prompt) can request a looser sandbox or a costlier model on an individual call. Verified against `codex --help` / `codex mcp-server --help` (codex-cli 0.124.0): no separate flag exists to hard-lock per-call arguments; `-c` only sets the config.toml-equivalent default the server starts with.
dataNote: Prompts, code, and file contents you send through this server leave this machine and are sent to OpenAI's Codex/ChatGPT backend under your ChatGPT subscription. This is a different vendor than Anthropic and a different data-handling relationship than any Anthropic-run tool in this catalog.

name: Dart & Flutter
description: Analyze and fix Dart & Flutter code, resolve symbols, fetch API docs, search pub.dev, manage pubspec.yaml dependencies, run tests, and format code — via Google's official dart mcp-server.
note: Provided by the Dart SDK — no separate install if `dart` (3.9+) is on your PATH. Experimental and evolving. Best used inside a Flutter/Dart project (a directory with pubspec.yaml). If your MCP client has trouble with workspace roots, add "--force-roots-fallback" to args.
package: dart mcp-server (bundled with the Dart SDK 3.9+; run via `dart`)
dataNote: Runs locally against your project's Dart/Flutter source; contacts pub.dev when searching packages or fetching docs. Requires the Dart SDK (3.9+) on your PATH.
